fit_quality: Normalized transport footprint E_H = V / (N × H × b) ≈ 116 hidden-width equivalents (H=2304, b=2 bytes BF16)
title: Fabric Exposure Fingerprint
sub_title: Topology Dictates Transport Risk Under Measured Bandwidth Caps
one_line_finding: The same measured fabric constraint has radically different application impact by topology: at 1M, configured-20G changes TP16/PP1 TTFT by ~+276.7%, while TP4/PP4 changes by only ~+3.9%.
large_number_caption: 1M c1 TTFT Degradation Under 20G Network Cap Sweep
observation: At 1M context on GCP_CAPPED_20G, TP16/PP1 TTFT degrades from 68.20s to 256.89s (+276.7% degradation; queue wait 0.022s). Under the exact same 20G cap, TP4/PP4 TTFT moves from 28.57s to 29.68s (+3.91% degradation). TP16/PP1 exposes communication across the VPC network where transport latency degrades with restricted bandwidth; TP4/PP4 restricts cross-node communication to point-to-point pipeline activation exchanges, keeping collective communication intra-node.
formula_derivation: Local transport sensitivity fit: TTFT(B) = T0 + V_exposed / B. Normalized transport footprint: E_H = V_exposed / (N_tokens * H * b) ≈ 116 bytes/token (H=2304, b=2 bytes BF16).
case_bench_network_provenance: tp4_pp4_dist, tp16_pp1_dist, tp4_pp2_dist, tp8_pp2_dist across GCP_NATIVE (173.6 Gbps), GCP_CAPPED_100G (56.8 Gbps), and GCP_CAPPED_20G (16.5 Gbps) at 1M context.
exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: N/A — E2E wall-clock client metric across 3 independent network environments.
boundary: This is a local empirical sensitivity coefficient over the measured bandwidth range. E_H = V / (N × H × b) represents a normalized hidden-width-equivalent exposure coefficient (H=2304, b=2 bytes BF16), NOT a literal transfer volume of 116 bytes/token.
required_follow_up_experiment: Validate with packet-level NIC queue counters and NCCL ring vs tree algorithm profiling under tc netem to isolate bufferbloat from serialization latency.
decision_changed: Do not size distributed inference from NIC/iperf capability alone; topology must be characterized under the target network and workload. In this campaign and workload regime, TP4/PP4 exhibited much lower network exposure than TP16/PP1.

fit_quality: Queue contribution closure: 96.4% to 97.5% of added TTFT is pure queue wait
title: Concurrency Value Destruction
sub_title: Queue Accounting Closure at 1M Extreme Context (Admission / SLO Risk)
one_line_finding: At 1M, added concurrency buys almost no output throughput but destroys user latency. On TP4, c4 adds only ~1.52% output throughput while TTFT becomes 2.48×, TPOT 26.15×, and mean queue residence reaches ~134.43 s.
observation: Once the severe 1M regime begins, added TTFT numerically tracks queue residence while KV remains far from exhaustion and preemptions stay zero. The detailed service-time/scheduler mechanism behind the queue buildup is not fully decomposed. On TP4, c4 TTFT reaches 231.27s with 134.43s mean queue residence, accounting for ~97.5% of TTFT growth over c1.

case_bench_network_provenance: tp4_1m_concurrency_extension and tp8_1m_concurrency_extension across 1m_c1, 1m_c2, 1m_c4 on SINGLE_NODE_LOCAL.
exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: N/A — E2E wall-clock client benchmark logs and server histogram telemetry.

fit_quality: FlashAttention scaling p ≈ 1.99 (O(N^2)); MoE p ≈ 0.96 (O(N)); KDA p ≈ 0.99 (O(N))
title: Long-Context Resource-Pressure Shift
sub_title: Attention Quadratic Scaling Replaces MoE / Linear Recurrence as Dominant Pressure
one_line_finding: Full-attention aggregate GPU work grows materially faster than KDA, MoE and NCCL between the matched 128K and 512K TP4/PP4 profiles. Re-evaluate the optimization target as context increases. This does not establish exclusive wall-clock critical-path ownership.
observation: Across 128K to 512K context scaling on TP4/PP4, FlashAttention aggregate GPU work scales by ~15.7× (scaling exponent p ≈ 1.99). In contrast, KDA linear recurrence scales by ~3.9× (p ≈ 0.99), MoE gating/routing scales by ~3.8× (p ≈ 0.96), NCCL scales by ~2.18×, and GEMM scales by ~5.25×. This demonstrates a shift in subsystem resource pressure as context extends.
formula_derivation: Scaling law exponent: p = ln(Work_512k / Work_128k) / ln(512 / 128) = ln(Ratio) / ln(4). Attention: ln(15.7)/1.386 ≈ 1.99; Linear: ln(3.9)/1.386 ≈ 0.99.
case_bench_network_provenance: tp4_pp4_dist across 128k_c1, 512k_c1, 1m_c1 on GCP_NATIVE, corroborated by Nsight profiler kernel traces.
exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: Median per-rank aggregate GPU work across valid rank Nsight trace profiles for FlashAttention, KDA recurrence, MoE routing, and GEMM kernels.
boundary: DERIVED / MODELED INTERPOLATION — NOT A MEASURED CRITICAL-PATH CROSSOVER. Cross-kernel overlap and CUDA stream concurrency prevent simple summation from representing absolute wall-clock time. Exponents are derived fits and the ~420K crossover is modeled.
required_follow_up_experiment: Run intermediate context sweeps (256K, 384K, 768K) with instrumented PyTorch NVTX ranges to measure true per-layer critical path wall-clock latency.
decision_changed: Full-attention aggregate GPU work grows materially faster than KDA, MoE and NCCL between the matched 128K and 512K TP4/PP4 profiles. Re-evaluate the optimization target as context increases. This does not establish exclusive wall-clock critical-path ownership.

fit_quality: Cold prefill p ≈ 1.4427 (R² = 0.9979); Warm prefix hit p ≈ 1.0013 (R² = 0.9935)
title: Prefix Reuse Changes Scaling Curve
sub_title: Full KV Hit Flattens Quadratic Context Penalty to Pure Linear Decode
one_line_finding: Reusing cached prefix state avoids recomputing the cached prefix portion, shifting median repeat TTFT from 94.23s to 2.61s at 1M (a 36.1× reduction).
large_number_caption: Prefix Warm-Hit vs Cold TTFT at 1M
observation: At 1M context on TP4/PP1, first-request (cold) TTFT is 94.23s, while repeated-request median TTFT drops to 2.61s (36.1× reduction). Across 8K, 128K, and 1M, prefix reuse avoids recomputing the cached prefix portion, shifting empirical scaling from prefill-dominated curves to lightweight lookup behavior.
formula_derivation: Power law fit: TTFT(N) = a * N^p. Cold prefill fit: p ≈ 1.4427 (R² = 0.9979). Warm prefix hit fit: p ≈ 1.0013 (R² = 0.9935).
exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: N/A — Client benchmark first-request vs repeated-request latency measurements.
boundary: Represents 100% full-prefix hit with near-zero generation length in tested benchmark runs. Real multi-turn chat exhibits variable prefix hit ratios, eviction dynamics, and interleaving under multi-tenant load.
required_follow_up_experiment: Benchmark partial prefix hit ratios (25%, 50%, 75%) and measure cache eviction latency under concurrent multi-tenant churn.
decision_changed: Repeated-prefix traffic can occupy a materially different latency regime, so prefix reuse should be treated as a workload-routing/caching lever. Optimize cache sizing to sustain high reuse for shared prefix workloads.

This suggests prompt-token rate is a more useful capacity coordinate than request rate for these measured prefill-heavy workloads; it is not established as a universal invariant.
observation: In open-loop capacity sweeps on TP4, prompt length differs 16× (8,192 vs 131,072 tokens), while sustained request rate diverges by ~18.2× (14.2 vs 0.78 req/s). Normalizing into prompt tokens/s collapses this divergence to ~27.5K vs ~24.2K tok/s (a ~14% spread across tested high-load points).
formula_derivation: Token admission capacity: C_tokens = RPS_saturation * Prompt_length. Spread = (27443 - 24248) / 27443 = 11.6%.

exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: N/A — Client open-loop arrival generator log analysis.
boundary: Derived from median achieved throughput across high-load points (1.00×, 1.10×, 1.25×) for 8K and 128K regimes on TP4 with chunk size 8192. It is not established as a universal invariant beyond tested prefill-dominated workloads.
required_follow_up_experiment: Execute open-loop sweeps on 512K and 1M context to test if the token absorption rate remains bounded between 20K–28K tok/s.

title: Parallelism Directional Elasticity
sub_title: Context Length Inverts TP/PP Scaling Leverage and GPU-Second Occupancy
one_line_finding: The measured return from additional TP changes sign with context (η = −0.245 @ 8K to +0.320 @ 1M), while PP scaling becomes progressively stronger over the tested long-context range (η = +0.631 to +0.879).
observation: On single-node TP4→TP8, scaling elasticity η is negative at short context (−0.245 @ 8K, −0.086 @ 128K), turning positive at long context (+0.184 @ 512K, +0.320 @ 1M). Conversely, distributed PP2→PP4 elasticity strengthens from +0.631 (128K) to +0.812 (512K) to +0.879 (1M). GPU-seconds/request frontier values span 373.0 to 1091.1 across tested topologies.
formula_derivation: Scaling elasticity: η = -[ln(TTFT_2 / TTFT_1)] / [ln(GPUs_2 / GPUs_1)]. Ideal linear scaling gives η = +1.0. GPU-seconds/request proxy = GPUs * TTFT_s.
case_bench_network_provenance: tp4_qualification, tp8_qualification, tp4_pp2_dist, tp4_pp4_dist, tp8_pp2_dist, tp16_pp1_dist across 8k_c1 and 1m_c1 on GCP_NATIVE.
exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: N/A — Wall-clock client latency multiplied by active GPU allocation.
boundary: GPU-seconds/request is an occupancy proxy across active GPU allocations, NOT a billing cost model. The exact compute/communication balance responsible for the elasticity transition remains partially resolved.
required_follow_up_experiment: Evaluate pipeline microbatch tuning under continuous streaming inference to reduce pipeline flush bubbles.
decision_changed: The measured return from additional TP changes sign with context, while PP scaling becomes progressively stronger over the tested long-context range. The exact compute/communication balance responsible for this transition remains only partially resolved. Evaluate scaling dimensions directionally by context.

fit_quality: NCCL 16K AllReduce (+94.7%) -> PyTorch Self CUDA (+132.2%) -> Nsight trace -> E2E TPOT (+41.9%)
title: TP Decode Evidence Chain
sub_title: 4-Layer Root-Cause Corroboration of Tensor-Parallel Decode Degradation
one_line_finding: Cross-tool evidence links 16 KiB NCCL latency (~19→37µs) and PyTorch AllReduce Self CUDA time (251.5→583.9ms across 7040 calls) directly to a +41.9% E2E TPOT increase (4.475→6.350ms) when widening TP4 to TP8 at 8K c1.
large_number_caption: 8K Decode TPOT Degradation from AllReduce Bus Contention
observation: Widening Tensor Parallelism from TP4 to TP8 at 8K degrades mean TPOT from 4.475ms to 6.350ms (+41.9%). The 4-layer evidence chain confirms: 1) Hardware NCCL 16K AllReduce latency doubles (19.0us → 37.0us); 2) PyTorch self-CUDA allreduce time increases by 2.32× (251.5ms → 583.9ms across 7040 calls); 3) Nsight decode kernel work confirms small-tensor synchronization overhead; 4) E2E TPOT reflects the aggregate slowdown.
formula_derivation: AllReduce cost: T_ar(M) = 2 * (P - 1) / P * (α + M / β). For small decode tensors (M=16KB), latency is latency-dominated by ring hops (P=8 vs P=4), doubling collective overhead.
case_bench_network_provenance: tp4_qualification vs tp8_qualification at 8k_c1 on SINGLE_NODE_LOCAL; nccl_points.csv for raw collectives.
exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: Exact PyTorch autograd trace self-CUDA summary across 7,040 allreduce calls per run.
boundary: Applies to decode phases with small token batches (batch tokens ≤ 16). Prefill phases with large batched tensors saturate bus bandwidth and exhibit different scaling characteristics.
required_follow_up_experiment: Profile custom allreduce kernels (OneShot / Tree-based) with CUDA graph capture to test if kernel launch overhead can be eliminated.
decision_changed: Do not assume wider TP improves interactive decode; for short decode-heavy work, collective synchronization can erase extra compute parallelism.

fit_quality: max_num_seqs: S < 0.05% (non-binding); chunk size: S = -27.12% (high leverage)
title: Runtime-Knob Derivative Fingerprint
sub_title: Inert Knobs (max_num_seqs) vs High-Leverage Knobs (chunk size) Characterization
one_line_finding: Some runtime knobs are completely non-binding (<0.05% change for max_num_seqs) while others have huge leverage: increasing chunk size from 4K to 16K cuts 1M TTFT by 27.1%.
observation: At 1M c4 on TP4, sweeping max_num_seqs 4→8→16 leaves TTFT virtually unchanged (~232.34s → ~232.36s → ~232.25s) because peak running sequences reached 2 and waiting reached 3, never binding on the configured limit. Conversely, sweeping chunk size 4K→8K→16K at 1M c1 reduces TTFT from 122.05s to 93.28s to 88.95s.
formula_derivation: Knob sensitivity: S_knob = (TTFT_max - TTFT_min) / TTFT_baseline. S_maxseq = (232.364 - 232.250) / 232.342 = 0.049%. S_chunk = (122.049 - 88.951) / 122.049 = 27.12%.
case_bench_network_provenance: tp4_1m_maxseq4, tp4_1m_maxseq8, tp4_1m_maxseq16, tp4_chunk4k, tp4_chunk8k, tp4_chunk16k on SINGLE_NODE_LOCAL.
exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: N/A — Client benchmark latency and server scheduler state logs.
boundary: Applies to measured single-node 1M configurations. 16K chunk size requires sufficient activation memory. In constrained configs, larger chunk budgets increase VRAM pressure during concurrent prefill.
required_follow_up_experiment: Sweep intermediate chunk sizes (10K, 12K, 14K) under concurrent multi-tenant load to identify the precise VRAM headroom inflection point.
decision_changed: Changing the chunk/token budget materially changes 1M c1 TTFT, indicating that this control is active in the measured regime; the exact kernel/scheduling mechanism should remain separate from the measured derivative. Allocate engineering tuning effort to chunk size and batched token budgets rather than non-binding sequence limits.

fit_quality: TP4/PP4 at 62.8% util is 2.39x faster than TP16/PP1 at 80.6% util (barrier spin)
title: Busy GPU != Efficient Serving
sub_title: High GPU Utilization Masks Severe Cross-Node Barrier Synchronization Spinning
one_line_finding: High GPU utilization is not proof of efficient compute: TP16 shows ~80.6% utilization but takes 68.2s TTFT at 1M, while TP4/PP4 shows ~62.8% utilization and delivers 28.6s TTFT (2.39× faster).
large_number_caption: TP16/PP1 vs TP4/PP4 Utilization vs Latency Paradox @ 1M
observation: At 1M context, cross-node TP16/PP1 shows ~80.6% mean GPU utilization while taking 68.20s TTFT (with ~77.6% AllReduce work share). In contrast, TP4/PP4 shows ~62.8% mean GPU utilization and delivers 28.57s TTFT (2.39× faster). Similar divergence occurs at 128K (75.4% / 4.41s vs 58.2% / 1.71s).
formula_derivation: Effective compute efficiency: Eff = Work_useful / (Utilization * Time). TP4/PP4 achieves 2.39x higher useful token progression per unit of time despite lower reported utilization.
case_bench_network_provenance: tp16_pp1_dist vs tp4_pp4_dist at 1m_c1 on GCP_NATIVE; corroborated by SCALEOUT_TELEMETRY_AUDIT.json.
exact_profile_rank_aggregation_rule: Mean GPU utilization logged across all 16 GPUs via nvidia-smi DCGM sampling at 100ms intervals.
boundary: Standard SMI/DCGM utilization metrics sample kernel activity without distinguishing between useful GEMM tensor core compute and communication or synchronization kernels.
required_follow_up_experiment: Deploy NVIDIA Nsight Systems timeline traces with PM counters (SM active vs Tensor Pipe active) to quantify exact non-spin FLOPS.
decision_changed: Do not use GPU utilization alone to choose or validate topology or capacity; combine it with TTFT, TPOT/goodput, queue residence, communication exposure, and profiler composition.

fit_quality: Reported KV% = 2.75% (PP divides KV), actual physical VRAM = 88.83 GiB (7.86 GiB margin)
title: KV Headroom != VRAM Headroom
sub_title: Pipeline Parallelism Divides KV Cache Usage While Physical VRAM Remains Near-Full
one_line_finding: Reported KV utilization drops materially with deeper PP (12.29% → 5.91% → 2.75%), while measured total GPU memory remains in the same high-80-GiB range (88.39 → 88.69 → 88.83 GiB). The observed PP×KV relationship is consistent with KV state being distributed across stages but does not establish the allocator's exact sharding rule.
large_number: 2.75% Reported KV vs 88.83 GiB Allocated VRAM
large_number_caption: Reported KV Headroom vs Physical VRAM Reality @ 1M
observation: At 1M c1 across pipeline stages (TP4/PP1, TP4/PP2, TP4/PP4), reported KV cache utilization drops from 12.29% to 5.91% to 2.75% (scaling roughly with 1/PP). However, peak measured GPU memory remains nearly constant at 88.39 GiB, 88.69 GiB, and 88.83 GiB across all stages, leaving narrow physical memory margin.
